messages:
Alex Chen: FYI — I clicked a link in an email from invoice@payservice.com and forwarded the original to security@redwood.com. It opened a Google-style consent screen asking to "verify workspace" and requested Drive + profile access. I clicked allow before I realized.
Maria Ruiz: Did you type your password or just approve the OAuth consent?
Alex Chen: I didn't type my password. I selected my corporate account and clicked allow on the consent screen.
Sam Kelleher: OK — treat this like OAuth compromise. @sec-bot please run token-audit for alex.chen@redwood.com and revoke any third-party grants.
sec-bot: token-audit started for alex.chen@redwood.com. Found 1 active grant for app `docs-helper.app` granted at 2026-03-17T10:12:00Z. Revocation initiated. (ref: /var/log/sec/token-audit/1769998888.log)
Erin Wang: Alex — change your password now, sign out of all sessions, and confirm 2FA is enabled.
Alex Chen: Done password reset and signed out of all web sessions. 2FA is on. I also forwarded the raw email; headers pasted below.
```
From: invoice@payservice.com
Received: from mail-12.example.net (mail-12.example.net [1.2.3.4])
Subject: Past Due Invoice #0342
List-Unsubscribe: <mailto:unsubscribe@payservice.com>
X-Originating-IP: 5.6.7.8
Message-ID: <CA+abc123@example.com>
```
Maria Ruiz: Thanks. Sandboxing the link/attachment now. Dropping the URL into the detonation lab.
sec-bot: sandbox result: URL redirect chain (3 hops) -> final host `docs-helper.app/oauth?client_id=xxxx`. Final payload: small HTML redirect + OAuth consent mimic. No binary. VirusTotal: 2/66 engines flagged. YARA: `suspicious_oauth_redirect` matched 2 rules.
Sam Kelleher: Good. Action plan: 1) Revoke the app consent in Google Workspace admin. 2) Block `docs-helper.app` at DNS/firewall and add to inbound email blocklist. 3) Create an inbound mail filter to drop messages with return-path invoice@payservice.com patterns. 4) Add detection rule for OAuth consent patterns and unusual grant timings.
Maria Ruiz: Created ticket INC-2026-134 and updated the incident tracker with timeline + sandbox log. Notifying SOC and platform to watch for any webhook callbacks or lateral activity.
Alex Chen: Do we need to rotate KMS keys or service principals? I had a browser session with some internal webapps open.
Erin Wang: No evidence of KMS/service account key exfiltration — the flow is OAuth consent delegation, not server-side key access. Still: rotate any long-lived tokens associated with your user and check service principals. Platform team: can you confirm no IAM role changes were observed?
Sam Kelleher: Platform confirmed no IAM binds or SA key usage from that account in the suspicious window. Logged remediation steps (revocations, DNS block, mail filter) and added a Hunts job to surface similar grants.
Maria Ruiz: We'll send a company awareness note tomorrow and schedule a short refresh on OAuth phishing. Post-mortem scheduled Monday. Thanks everyone, and thanks @Alex for forwarding the email quickly :thumbsup:
